subject: chemistry
title: Variable oxidation states
key_idea: Transition metals form ions in several oxidation states, each with its own colour. Whether one state can be turned into another is predicted from standard electrode potentials: a reaction is feasible when the overall cell potential is positive. Redox titrations with manganate(VII) use these changes to find concentrations.

blocks.text: Vanadium shows four oxidation states in solution, each with a different colour. Zinc in acid reduces them step by step.

diagram.alt: Pick an oxidation state of vanadium to see its ion and colour.
diagram.prompt: Pick an oxidation state of vanadium

items: The Eᶿ of Zn²⁺/Zn (−0.76 V) is more negative than all three vanadium couples, so zinc can reduce vanadium all the way from +5 to +2.
Colour changes in order: yellow, blue, green, violet.
A weaker reducing agent stops earlier. Its Eᶿ must be more negative than the couple you want it to reduce.
Vanadium: +5 yellow, +4 blue, +3 green, +2 violet.
Zinc in acid reduces +5 to +2.
A reducing agent works on a couple only if its Eᶿ is more negative.

blocks.text: A reaction is feasible if its overall cell potential is positive. This uses the same rule for every redox pair.

blocks.label: Cell potential
where: Eᶿ(reduction) = the more positive couple, where reduction happens.
Eᶿ(oxidation) = the less positive couple, where oxidation happens.

items.text: Can Fe³⁺ oxidise I⁻? Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ is +0.77 V and I₂/I⁻ is +0.54 V.

items.lead: Choose the more positive as reduction.
items.text: Fe³⁺ is reduced to Fe²⁺. I⁻ is oxidised to I₂.
Eᶿcell = +0.77 − (+0.54) = +0.23 V. Positive, so the reaction is feasible.

items: The redox potential for a metal ion going from a higher to a lower oxidation state depends on pH and on the ligand.
A ligand or pH that stabilises the higher state more makes Eᶿ more negative, so the higher state is a weaker oxidising agent. Feasibility can then change.
A positive Eᶿcell says the reaction is possible, not that it is fast.
Eᶿcell = Eᶿ(reduction) − Eᶿ(oxidation); positive means feasible.
Eᶿ values change with pH and ligand.
Feasible does not mean fast.

blocks.text: These interconversions and colour changes are the ones you need to know.

blocks.label: Chromate(VI) and dichromate(VI) equilibrium
where: Chromium stays +6. This is an acid-base change, not redox.

items: Fe²⁺ (pale green) is oxidised to Fe³⁺ (yellow-brown) by H⁺/MnO₄⁻. Purple manganate(VII) turns colourless.
Fe³⁺ is reduced to Fe²⁺ by I⁻. The iodide is oxidised to iodine, which makes the solution brown.
Cu²⁺ is reduced to Cu⁺ by I⁻. A white precipitate of CuI forms in brown iodine solution.
In water Cu⁺ is unstable and disproportionates: 2Cu⁺ → Cu²⁺ + Cu.
Disproportionation is the oxidation and reduction of the same element in one reaction.
Dichromate(VI) is orange; Cr³⁺ is green; chromate(VI) is yellow.
Fe²⁺ is oxidised by MnO₄⁻/H⁺; Fe³⁺ is reduced by I⁻.
Cu⁺ disproportionates in water to Cu²⁺ and Cu.

blocks.text: Manganate(VII) titrations find the amount of a reducing agent. It is its own indicator: the end point is the first permanent pink.

items: Use dilute sulfuric acid, which gives the H⁺. Do not use hydrochloric acid, because MnO₄⁻ oxidises Cl⁻.
Ethanedioate is warmed to about 60 °C, because the reaction is slow at first.

diagram.alt: Calculate the concentration of iron(II) from a manganate(VII) titration.
diagram.question: 25.0 cm³ of Fe²⁺(aq) needs {v} cm³ of 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ potassium manganate(VII) for complete reaction. MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. Calculate the concentration of Fe²⁺ in mol dm⁻³.

items: Tollens' reagent contains [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺. It is reduced to silver: [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ + e⁻ → Ag + 2NH₃.
Aldehydes reduce it and give a silver mirror. Ketones do not. This distinguishes the two.
MnO₄⁻ : Fe²⁺ is 1 : 5. MnO₄⁻ : C₂O₄²⁻ is 2 : 5.
The end point is the first permanent pink.
Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror with aldehydes only.

checks.q: Describe the colour changes seen when an acidified solution containing VO₂⁺ is reduced with excess zinc.
checks.a: Yellow, to blue (VO²⁺), to green (V³⁺), to violet (V²⁺).

checks.q: Eᶿ(Cr₂O₇²⁻/Cr³⁺) = +1.33 V and Eᶿ(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V. Is the oxidation of Fe²⁺ by dichromate(VI) in acid feasible? Explain.
checks.a: Eᶿcell = +1.33 − (+0.77) = +0.56 V. This is positive, so the reaction is feasible.

checks.q: 24.0 cm³ of 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ MnO₄⁻ reacts with 25.0 cm³ of Fe²⁺(aq). Calculate the concentration of Fe²⁺.

items: Fe²⁺ is oxidised with H⁺/MnO₄⁻ and Fe³⁺ is reduced with I⁻.
Cr³⁺ is oxidised with H₂O₂/OH⁻ and Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced with Zn/H⁺.
Cu²⁺ is reduced with I⁻, and Cu⁺ readily disproportionates to Cu²⁺ and Cu in aqueous conditions.
The equations are built from half-equations and oxidation numbers, rather than learned.
Dichromate(VI) is reduced to Cr³⁺ and Cr²⁺ by zinc in acidic conditions, as Eᶿ shows.
Cr₂O₇²⁻ is made by oxidising Cr³⁺ with hydrogen peroxide in alkaline conditions, then acidifying.
Use the equilibrium 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O to explain the conversion of chromate(VI) and dichromate(VI).
Vanadium(IV), (III) and (II) are formed by reducing vanadate(V) ions with zinc in acidic solution.
Calculations on the titrations of Fe²⁺ and C₂O₄²⁻ with MnO₄⁻, and on similar redox reactions.
Tollens' reagent distinguishes aldehydes from ketones.
Use Eᶿ values from a data booklet to predict whether a redox reaction of a transition element or its ions is feasible.
Eᶿcell = Eᶿ(reduction) − Eᶿ(oxidation), and a positive value means feasible.
